# Decisions: record-integrity

- 2026-08-01T17:31:20.624Z — chose **Derive a session's home initiative from the event logs themselves — scan for the session's earliest session_started, checking the branch-bound initiative first and only falling through to siblings on a miss** over A new .sofar/sessions.json index mapping session_id to slug, written at registration and read by hooks because The home is ALREADY in the truth log — session_started names it uniquely — so an index file would be duplicated state that can desync, needs pruning (99 sessions and counting), and forces a SPEC Record-layout change plus a gitignore decision (routing is a local runtime fact, but .sofar/ is committed wholesale). Deriving costs one file read on the common path (branch is correct → hit on the first log checked) and only pays the sibling scan in exactly the case where a misroute would otherwise have happened; total log volume is ~350KB. It is also self-healing: sessions registered before this fix get pinned correctly with no migration. Same philosophy as reading git state rather than logging it — a fact with an authoritative home is read, never copied.
- 2026-08-01T17:41:22.869Z — chose **Pin start_session to the session home as well as the hooks — branch resolution now applies only when `initiative` is explicit or the session has no home** over Pinning hooks alone (the original Phase 1 scope), or using envelope.source to tell a deliberate re-home from a misroute because Measuring the 14 double-registrations in this repo inverted the hypothesis: 11 are hook-then-claude-code across two initiatives, i.e. the tear is NOT mostly a mid-session branch switch but lazy registration racing start_session — the hook registers in the branch's initiative, the binding moves, and start_session registers the SAME id again elsewhere. Hook pinning alone would have left those 11 intact. The source-based heuristic was rejected by the same data: the second registration is usually claude-code, so treating claude-code as deliberate would suppress 11 of 14 real splits.
- 2026-08-01T17:44:11.519Z — chose **Accept the 21 pre-existing splits as history — no correction-event repair — and grade doctor's session-routing findings by LIVENESS: FAIL only when a split involves a session still open, WARN when every session in it has ended** over Repairing the splits with correction events, or leaving every split at FAIL because User ruling: the pin handles everything going forward, so retro-repair buys nothing. But a permanently red doctor trains people to ignore it, and 0/3450 events carry any self-evident misplacement marker (envelope.initiative always matches its directory), so repair would be inferential anyway — asserting a guess as a correction event is worse than leaving accurate history. Liveness is the honest severity axis: an ended split is settled and unfixable by construction, while an open one is a pre-fix session still actively tearing and worth blocking on.
- 2026-08-01T17:47:16.664Z — chose **Repair scope = close the one abandoned session (40742c6d in harness-build) and nothing else; reattributing the 780 leaked events is rejected as unsound** over Voiding leaked events in their wrong initiative and re-appending them into the right one because Reattribution is not expressible in this log's semantics. correction events VOID by ref (fold.ts pass 1) — they delete, they cannot move — and replay order is normatively ulid order (task 13.1, D-sync-1) so replicas converge. A re-appended event therefore carries a fresh ulid encoding now and sorts to the END of the target log, folding after that session's session_ended and after every task that was active at the real time. That fabricates a timeline that never happened, which is strictly worse than accurate history filed in the wrong place. Closing 40742c6d is different in kind: the session genuinely ended without a write-back in July, so session_closed asserts only what is true, and it takes doctor from 1 FAIL to exit 0.
- 2026-08-02T08:36:14.586Z — chose **Bound the parallel-wrap window by this session's own liveness (skip entirely when me.ended is set), and compose next_action + push state before the summary so the summary absorbs the leftover budget** over Adding a "already told you" marker to suppress repeats, or widening the 420-char budget because The defect was not repetition, it was the window: checking only s.ended >= me.started bounds below and not above, so an ENDED session kept reporting siblings that wrapped after it closed, forever, on every prompt. An ended session is not working and has no window for anything to have wrapped inside — one guard removes the whole class. Keeping it stateless preserves the design property that made the line cheap. Budget order is the same kind of fix: the summary is the least actionable field and was rendering first, so it clipped away the next action; reserving the tail costs nothing and cannot regress.
- 2026-08-03T09:08:56.759Z — chose **start_session adopts an ENDED session (pin-only, no append, history untouched), and the parallel-wrap window anchors on this session's last write-back rather than its liveness** over Reopening an ended session at fold level by clearing ended/summary, or keeping the 0.12.1 rule that suppressed the line for any ended session because Tracing a real parallel session (3c1146f3 rewrote README.md and wrapped at 09:00:38 while 01KZ3DKC63 was live, with nothing reported) showed the 0.12.1 guard was treating a symptom. Defects 1 and 2 were one bug: the phantom sibling was the agent's OWN replacement identity, minted only because start_session refused an ended id. Fixing the identity removes the phantom, and the window then needs a real bound — the last write-back, which is the same "since I absorbed the record" frame the drift counter uses, and unlike `started` it actually closes. Fold-level reopen was rejected because clearing summary to re-arm the Stop gate erases the prior write-back from sessions/<id>.md while its event still stands in the log.
